chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Muhammad al-Halabi who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Stone when one is not able to touch it and there is much congestion, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the old man, the weak, and the sick, they are excused; and I do not like that you leave touching it unless you have no choice.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on touching the Black Stone if one is weak or crowded?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while touching the Black Stone is highly recommended (mustahabb) for the general public, it is excused for the elderly, weak, or ill, yet he personally dislikes omitting it unless congestion makes it unavoidable. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly balance between adhering to ritual etiquette and accommodating physical limitations during the intense crowding of Hajj. It underscores the principle that the spiritual intent behind the act remains valid even if the physical contact is missed due to necessity.
